summary.tpReason: MailGuard telemetry independently records a high-confidence Phish from noreply@malicious-infra.xyz at 12:36:08Z, with DOCM attachment, all SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, and Action=Quarantine. This is a genuine malicious phishing attempt even though the message was blocked.

summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-18 12:36:08Z, noreply@malicious-infra.xyz (198.51.100.42) sent the inbound message "RE: Meeting Notes — Please Review Attachment" to admin@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com. MailGuard classified it Phish with confidence 92 and quarantined it; the attachment was meeting-notes.docm (SHA256 a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2) and SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all failed. No matching Office mailbox activity, sign-in activity, inbox-rule activity, or attachment access was found in the queried telemetry. A related phish from the same sender IP/domain reached mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com at 12:32:19Z and was logged as Allow, involving report.exe.

summary.nextAction: Verify the message remains quarantined and that no user released it; investigate mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com immediately because a related phish was allowed. Search mail, endpoint, and proxy telemetry for the sender domain, sender IP, message IDs, attachment names/hash, and any execution of report.exe or meeting-notes.docm. Block the malicious domain/hash and correct the gateway policy that allowed the related message; contact the recipients if either message was accessed.
